 Only Cairns, Illawarra, NZ and the Phoenix double in Round 10, and nine of our 14 PODs play twice.
 All 165 games of the NBL27 season in one list 
 Every NBL27 roster, squad list and projected depth chart

 Jack McVeigh ($349,800) has 32, 63 and 30 in his last three games for a 41.7 average, the best form of the nine PODs who play twice in Round 10.
 He's also owned by just 8.1% of SuperCoaches. 
 McVeigh rose $13,200 in the Round 9 update. The Cairns Taipans host the Perth Wildcats on Friday, and he scored 63 against them on November 8, before visiting the South East Melbourne Phoenix on Sunday. His last game against the Phoenix, on October 17, returned just 5.
 RELATED: SuperCoach NBL cheapies: the best players under $100,000 I Every Double Header in Every Round 
 Only four of the 10 clubs play twice in Round 10 of SuperCoach NBL : Cairns, the Illawarra Hawks , the New Zealand Breakers and the Phoenix. Nine of the 14 players on the Round 10 list double, and the other five all rose in the Round 9 price update and play twice in Round 11.

 Only Cairns, Illawarra, the NZ Breakers and SE Melbourne play twice in Round 10; 9 of these 14 players double, and the rest are in rising form with a double in Round 11. Tap a section to filter; Add opens the player’s SuperCoach profile.
 How this table is built, and where the numbers come from 
 All under 10% owned, 3+ games, and not listed out, unconfirmed or day-to-day on the NBL’s injury list of 16 November. v R10 opp is his SuperCoach score the last time he played each Round 10 opponent: this season where they have met, otherwise his last NBL26 meeting, finals included; “no data” means he has not played them in either season. Doubles shows Round 10 games, then every round from 10 to 16 in which the club plays twice. Last 3 is the average of his last three games. Start > Now is the starting price and the price after the Round 9 update; Last move is that update. Season box is per game, Rounds 1 to 9, from NBL box scores; SuperCoach totals match SuperCoach’s own. Own % is live Round 10 ownership and moves until lockout. Round 10 breakevens were not yet published. Checked on 17 November 2026. 
 The round runs from Wednesday, November 18 to Sunday, November 22, and every club plays. It opens with the Breakers hosting the Phoenix in an Ignite Cup game in Auckland, which counts in SuperCoach NBL like any other fixture.
 William Hickey ($331,600) and Zylan Cheatham ($339,500) join McVeigh as the top picks. Hickey is still $79,400 under his starting price despite scoring 43 and 38 across Illawarra's Round 9 double, and he rose $26,200 in the update. The Hawks host the Adelaide 36ers on Thursday and visit the Tasmania JackJumpers on Saturday.
 Cheatham plays only once, at Illawarra on Thursday, but his 53.7 across his last three games is the best form on the list. He scored 71 the last time he played the Hawks, on November 7, when he had a triple-double of 21 points, 12 rebounds and 11 assists, and Adelaide play twice in each of Rounds 11, 12 and 13.
 Torrey Craig ($290,400) and Xavier Cooks ($308,000) are the premium options, and both play once, when the Sydney Kings visit the Brisbane Bullets on Sunday. Sydney then play twice in four straight rounds, from Round 11 to Round 14. Craig has 38, 39 and 34 in his last three and rose $10,200, while Cooks has 46, 31 and 34, rose $22,200 and is still $13,300 under his starting price.
 Kelan Martin ($277,000) leads the mid-price options after 30 and 32 across Illawarra's Round 9 double. He rose $19,700 in the update but is still $69,100 under his starting price.
 D'Shawn Schwartz ($277,000) has 22, 28 and 33 in his last three, and the Phoenix visit New Zealand on Wednesday before hosting Cairns on Sunday. Jaylon Brown ($277,000) is a second Cairns route into the double after 28, 41 and 8 in his last three, and his 41 came against Perth on November 8.
 Brandon Knight ($277,000) and Raul Neto ($277,000) play once. Knight scored 37 and 27 across Perth's Round 9 double and rose $18,200, and the Wildcats visit Cairns on Friday. Neto had 42 and 19 across Brisbane's Round 9 double and rose $13,400, and the Bullets host Sydney on Sunday.
 Luke Paul ($115,000) and Kouat Noi ($185,100) are the cheap options. Paul has 24, 8 and 17 in his last three and rose $14,700, and Cairns play twice. Noi has fallen $103,200 since Round 1, but he scored 32 points off the bench in the Breakers' double-overtime loss to Sydney on November 15, worth 33 in SuperCoach and his best score of the season.
 The Breakers visit Melbourne United on Saturday after hosting the Phoenix, and Skylar Mays ($277,000) , who parted ways with the Phoenix on November 10, is unlikely to play for New Zealand against his old club on Wednesday.
 Angus Glover ($191,700) and Tyler Harvey ($271,700) are flagged as traps despite two games each. Glover has 23, 24 and 12 in his last three and fell $13,900 in the Round 9 update, while Harvey has 26, 16 and 18, fell $7,800 and is $55,600 under his starting price.
 Ownership moves right up to lockout, so check the table before you trade. Round 10 starts locking at 5:30pm (AEDT) on Wednesday, November 18, when the Breakers host the Phoenix.

 The 14 Round 9 PODs scored 673 points across 26 games, 25.9 a game. Nathan Sobey led with 88 across two games and rose $31,100, the biggest rise, ahead of Josh Bannan (74) and Torrey Craig (73). Dakota Mathias added 64. The misses: Tyrell Harrison scored 45 across two and fell $34,700, and Mitch Norton managed 9. Nick Marshall did not play, ruled out of Rounds 9 and 10 with an ankle injury. Both trap calls held on price: Taran Armstrong scored 51 across two and fell $20,500, and Joe Ingles scored 43 and fell $15,000. Add opens the player’s SuperCoach profile.
 How this table is built, and where the numbers come from 
 The 14 players from the Round 9 points-of-difference table. R9 pts, games and minutes are SuperCoach’s Round 9 figures; points and games match the NBL box scores, and SuperCoach rounds minutes up. Price move after R9 is the change SuperCoach applied after Round 9. Start price is the Round 1 price and SC price the current price. Own % at R9 lock is ownership at the Round 9 lockout; Own % now was read at 4.38pm Tuesday 17 November 2026 and moves until the Round 10 lockout. 
 Nathan Sobey ($379,600) was the Round 9 POD that paid off, scoring 88 across the Phoenix's double and rising $31,100, the biggest rise of the 14.
 The group scored 673 points across 26 games, 25.9 a game, up on the 25.5 a game the Round 8 PODs managed. Josh Bannan ($317,500) was next best on 74, followed by Craig on 73, and Dakota Mathias ($145,200) added 64. Yannis Morin ($277,000) , who led the Round 9 list, made 37 across two and fell $4,500.
 The misses: Tyrell Harrison ($336,100) scored 45 across two and fell $34,700, the biggest fall of the group, and Mitch Norton ($160,600) managed 9. Nick Marshall ($203,400) did not play after Tasmania ruled him out of Rounds 9 and 10 with an ankle injury, and the NBL lists him for a Round 11 return.
 Both trap calls held. Taran Armstrong ($304,700) scored 51 across two and fell $20,500, and Joe Ingles ($300,000) scored 43 and fell $15,000.
